title: Laser hair removal
what: A laser heats the hair roots and damages them. Hair gradually falls out and then grows back less.
why: When you want to remove unwanted hair on the body or face for a long time.
duration: one session takes from 10 minutes to an hour, depending on the area; a course is usually 6 to 10 sessions
tell_doctor: Medicines that make you sensitive to the sun
Cold sores, if the area near the lips is treated
A tendency to dark spots or scars

prepare.title: Shaving
prepare.text: Usually you shave the area 1 to 2 days before. Do not pluck or wax. The root must stay in place.

prepare.title: Sun
prepare.text: For 2 weeks before, do not tan or use self-tanner.

prepare.title: Skin
prepare.text: On the day, do not put creams or deodorant on the area.

steps: The specialist checks your skin and hair
Sometimes a cooling gel is applied
The laser is passed over the area, section by section
The skin is cooled, and a soothing product is applied
feel: It feels like a rubber band snapping on the skin, or warmth
Sensitive areas may feel more unpleasant
Afterward, redness and slight swelling around the hairs for a few hours
after: For a few days, do not tan, and use sunscreen
For 1 to 2 days, avoid saunas, steam rooms, and pools
After 1 to 3 weeks, the treated hairs start to fall out. This is normal
Your next session is after the time the specialist tells you
red_flags: Blisters, severe pain, or a burn
Spots on the skin that do not go away

faq.q: Will the hair be gone for good?
faq.a: Usually there is much less hair, and it is thinner and lighter. Sometimes a top-up session once a year is needed.

faq.q: Why are so many sessions needed?
faq.a: The laser works only on hairs that are growing now. Others are resting and are treated next time.

reminders.text: Laser hair removal tomorrow. Shave the area, avoid tanning, and do not put on cream.
